## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Uposathāvimānavatthu* (Vv 24) is a verse text belonging to the *Vimānavatthu* in the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral; Lim 2009]. Structured around a question-and-answer exchange between the Venerable Mahā-Moggallāna and an enskied female deva, the text recounts the past human life of the laywoman Uposathā [Lim 2009]. Having frequently heard descriptions of the heavenly Nandana grove, she set her mind upon it with longing (*tattha cittaṃ paṇidhāya*), which resulted in her rebirth in that celestial realm [Lim 2009]. However, she expresses regret for having aimed her mind at an inferior destination (*hīne cittaṃ paṇidhāya*) instead of cultivating it further toward higher spiritual attainments [SuttaCentral; Lim 2009]. Modern scholarship has examined the text as an illustration of the operation of resolve and aspiration (*paṇidhi*) in early Buddhist rebirth doctrine [Lim 2009].

The text shares extensive formulaic and verse material across the Pali canon and commentaries. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates 184 matching passages across 19 Pali texts, with the largest internal parallels occurring in the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Soṇadinnāvimānavatthu* (Vv 23), *Lakhumāvimānavatthu* (Vv 19), *Uttarāvimānavatthu* (Vv 15), and *Nimijātaka* (Ja 541) [DharmaNexus]. Canonical and commentarial cross-references also connect it to the *Catumahārājasutta* (AN 3.37), *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, and *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus records low-scoring automatic alignments with the Chinese *Dīrgha Āgama* (T 1) and *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26) [DharmaNexus].
